title: Three-Shot
description: A three-shot, or three shot, frames three principal subjects together, usually so alliances and the odd one out are readable in the blocking. It is a group sentence of three, not three singles cut together.

sections.title: Narrative function

blocks.text: A trio has politics. Two against one, a hinge person in the middle, a late arrival who splits a pair: the triangle is the story.

If you only cover this as ping-pong singles, the audience never sees who is left out in real space. It is the wrong tool when there are four or more as a unit, or when the scene has collapsed to a pair.
It is also the wrong tool if you line three heads up with equal light and equal height and call that drama. Someone should own a peak of the triangle, or stand in the cold of it.

sections.title: How it works

blocks.text: Arrange three bodies as a triangle in depth or across the frame, not a flat police lineup unless the story is a firing squad. Triangular Composition helps, but blocking comes first: seats, levels, who faces whom.
Keep all three faces or postures readable enough to compare. Prompt: Three-shot of [Subject] in a triangular group, alliances and the odd one out readable in blocking.

sections.title: When to use it

blocks.text: Use it when a trio has politics: three gunmen, three people at a verdict, a couple plus the person who should not be there. Do not flatten them into equal portraits, and do not use a three-shot for a crowd.

sections.title: Compared with similar shots

blocks.text: A Two-Shot is a pair; adding a third changes the grammar. A Group Shot holds a small ensemble larger than three as a relational unit.
A Master Shot may be a three-shot if the whole action is those three bodies. Do not treat three-shot as a synonym for any wide with extra extras.

sections.title: In film

blocks.text: The Good, the Bad and the Ugly is the textbook trio: three men, three distances, one cemetery geometry. The standoff only works because all three remain comparable in shared frames before the eyes take over.
Grammar: three principals, readable alliance.

sections.title: Prompt it

blocks.text: Name three and the triangle. Example: Three-shot of [Subject] in a triangular group, alliances and the odd one out readable in blocking.
Specify who is isolated by height, light, or gap. For video, a small blocking shift (one step back) should change the politics without a cut.

sections.title: What usually goes wrong

blocks.text: The usual wrong cousin is a Two-Shot that crops the third, or a Group Shot with extras filling the sides. The tell is two faces and a shoulder, or a crowd.
Fix: three principals, triangular blocking, one of them slightly out.

sections.title: Questions

blocks.text: What is Three-Shot in film?
A three-shot frames three principal people in one composition so their alliances, blocking, and who is left out are readable. It is not three close-ups in a row.
Three-Shot vs Two-Shot
A two-shot is a pair and the space between them. A three-shot adds a third principal and a triangle of politics. If the third person is only an out-of-focus extra, you still have a two-shot.
When should I use Three-Shot?
Use it when the scene's power is three-way: alliances, a hinge, an odd one out. Do not use it for a pair, and do not use it as a stand-in for a larger ensemble.
How do I prompt Three-Shot for AI image or video?
Write Three-shot of [Subject] in a triangular group, alliances and the odd one out readable in blocking. Name who is isolated. Keep all three readable.
